correctness.rationale: Every independent (n-2)-subset of root incidence vectors corresponds to a two-component spanning forest with Gram determinant s(n-s). For unicyclic connected n-vertex G with c-cycle, selecting n-2 edges by removing either a bridge and cycle edge (c such sets per bridge), or two cycle edges (interval components A_{i,k}); deleting two bridges leaves a cycle and contributes zero. Therefore S(G)=2c sum_bridge sqrt(s_e(n-s_e))+sum_{i,k}sqrt(A_{i,k}(n-A_{i,k})). Each bridge s_e between 1 and n-c has sqrt(s(n-s))>=sqrt(n-1), equality only s=1, forcing all off-cycle vertices direct leaves. The strictly concave sum of cyclic interval terms reaches its minimum at a vertex of the simplex a_i>=1,sum=n, i.e. all leaves at one cycle vertex, proving the global bound and rigidity. Inside direct-leaf family, Jensen gives sharp balanced upper bound when c|n. Because f_double_prime<=-2/n, strong concavity yields the exact quadratic stability deficit. Independent all-integer direct-leaf allocations for (n,c)=(6,3),(8,4),(9,3) confirm extrema and deficit; infinite proof is symbolic.
residual_risks: General unicyclic maximum is NOT claimed; c not dividing n makes the stated balanced upper bound unattained. n>c>=3, unit edge roots, intrinsic Euclidean metric in sum-zero hyperplane.

evidence: Joós–Lángi Corollary 1 proves V_{n-2} as sum of independent (n-2)-subset parallelepiped volumes. For unicyclic G, this becomes bridge cuts and two-cycle-edge interval cuts. Its Theorem 3 has unrestricted regular extremizers, whereas here the graph-restricted minimizer is cycle-star and the direct-leaf upper bound uses Jensen with equality at balanced a_i.

The new optimization relies on the strict concavity of sqrt(s(n-s)) and the integer leaf allocation geometry, not direct substitution into a published extremal theorem.

originality.rationale: Joós–Lángi Corollary 1, read in full from accessible arXiv HTML, establishes the general zonotope intrinsic-volume generator-subset sum. Their §3.1 Theorem 3 optimizes intrinsic volumes over all d or d+1 segment zonotopes at fixed volume and has regular extremizers in those unrestricted classes. It does NOT imply the sharp MINIMUM within the restrictive unit graphic-incidence unicyclic class at fixed n and cycle length c, whose extremizer is a highly asymmetric cycle-star, nor the balanced direct-leaf constrained MAXIMUM with explicit variance deficit. Independent graph-forest concavity proof is substantive. Prior results about trees, abstract graphic matroids, and zonotope deformation cones do not determine this metric classification. Best-of-knowledge PASS, with graph cut-energy risks.
residual_risks: A graph-cut invariant or chemical-graph index under different names might encode the same cycle-star surface-area optimization.
Full literature over all fixed-cycle-length cut-energy extremizers is not exhausted; the current proof uses a known general intrinsic-volume identity.

value.rationale: Sharp full-class metric minimum, unique extremizing rooted-tree arrangement, opposite sharp constrained maximum, and a quantitative stability inequality on leaf allocations separate Euclidean geometry from common matroid and constant volume. Those are natural and potentially reusable graph/zonotope comparison benchmarks, not mechanical duplication of the forest-volume formula.
residual_risks: The exact general surface-area formula is a specialization of established zonotope intrinsic-volume decomposition; new value lies in optimization, equality and stability.

final_claim: For n>c>=3 unit unicyclic graphical zonotopes, the sharp intrinsic surface-area minimum is 2c(n-c)sqrt(n-1)+2 sum_{k=1}^{c-1}(c-k)sqrt(k(n-k)), uniquely all leaves at one cycle vertex; among direct-leaf graphs the balanced upper bound 2c(n-c)sqrt(n-1)+n sum_{k=1}^{c-1}sqrt(k(c-k)) has equality iff c|n with uniform allocations and a stated strong-concavity quadratic deficit.
limitations: No maximum among all rooted unicyclic graphs; discrete balanced upper bound may be strict if n not divisible by c.
Earlier graph-cut-energy/isoperimetric literature could express same optimization, residual priority risk.
